hypothesis: Species-specific input relevance improves local correction transfer compared with a shared global distance.
changed_factor: Fixed species-specific diagonal feature weights learned from training-only rank association
calibration: 50k library excluding all 1024 T query IDs; same 48976 rows for both library sizes; U/D excluded
metric: w_ij = 0.1 + 0.9*119*rho_ij^2/sum_j(rho_ij^2); average-rank Spearman correlation; all-one fallback for zero sum
controls: all-one global 119-feature distance with exact prior graph parity
search: FP64 direct differences after sqrt-weight scaling; stable library-order ties; dataset-qualified self exclusion
primary_comparison: correction transfer on U and D, separately for k=1 and k=8 and both library sizes/seeds

outcomes.gain_with_less_damage_both_seeds: Species relevance is supported for these diagnostic transfers; consider one trained feature-local method, not a deployed lookup.
outcomes.gain_but_below_base: Metric contains additional signal but is insufficient; no promotion or automatic library growth.
outcomes.no_consistent_gain: Close this simple marginal-rank metric recipe; do not tune its floor on D.
outcomes.training_only_gain: Association did not transfer; no held-out or general applicability claim.

limitations: Marginal monotone correlations can miss interactions and nonmonotone dependence
10k searches use metric calibration beyond the 10k library
T query labels are excluded from metric fitting, but the frozen base saw them
U and D are repeatedly inspected development diagnostics
